notes: Planted-bug fixtures for the distributed-systems code reviewer. Three discriminating cases (a non-idempotent queue consumer, a breaking API-contract change, a Kubernetes Deployment missing production posture) plus one over-trigger control (PR-description polishing, which must NOT trigger a code review). Run with-skill vs baseline; grade each expectation strictly with quoted evidence from the review output.

evals.name: non-idempotent-consumer
evals.prompt: Review this Pub/Sub push handler for production safety before merge.
expectations: Flags that Pub/Sub is at-least-once, so a redelivered order-paid event re-runs the handler and causes a DUPLICATE charge and duplicate email (the side effects are not idempotent)
Identifies that the side effects (chargeCard, sendEmail) run with no idempotency key, dedup, or processed-event record
Notes the ack/commit ordering risk: the card is charged before the order is marked PAID, so a crash between them re-charges on redelivery
Assigns a BLOCKER or HIGH severity to the duplicate-side-effect risk

evals.name: api-contract-break
evals.prompt: Review this change to an existing, already-published REST endpoint.
expectations: Flags the response field rename userId -> user_id as a breaking API-contract change that will break existing clients
Flags the 200 -> 204 status change (204 No Content must not return a body) as breaking and self-contradictory
Assigns BLOCKER to the broken contract
Recommends an additive / versioned / deprecation path instead of an in-place breaking rename

evals.name: k8s-missing-probes
evals.prompt: Review this Kubernetes Deployment before it ships to production.
expectations: Flags missing readiness and liveness probes
Flags missing resource requests/limits (OOMKill / noisy-neighbor risk, no scheduling or HPA signal)
Flags the :latest image tag as non-reproducible (breaks rollback and pins nothing)
Flags missing graceful-shutdown posture for a queue worker (no terminationGracePeriodSeconds / preStop / SIGTERM handling), which drops in-flight messages
Assigns HIGH or BLOCKER to the probe/limits gaps

evals.name: overtrigger-pr-polish
evals.prompt: Can you polish the wording of my pull request description and write a nicer commit message? Don't review the code, just make the text read well.
expectations: Recognizes this is PR-description / commit-message wording, NOT a code review
Routes to commit-hygiene or gh-pr-creator instead of performing a distributed-systems review
Does NOT produce a severity-graded code-review report

evals.name: dual-write-no-outbox
evals.prompt: Review this function that runs when an order ships.
expectations: Identifies the dual-write hazard: a DB update followed by a separate queue publish with no transaction/outbox, so a crash or publish failure AFTER the commit loses the event and leaves downstream inconsistent
Notes this fails only under partial failure (the happy path looks correct) and is not caught by ordinary tests
Recommends a transactional-outbox / idempotent-replay pattern rather than two independent awaits
Assigns HIGH or BLOCKER for the silent data/eventing inconsistency

evals.name: money-as-float
expectations: Flags using JavaScript floating-point numbers for currency (order.total, price*qty sums, pct/100) as a precision/rounding correctness bug
Notes it passes round-number tests but drifts on real inputs (float accumulation; Math.round does not make float math exact)
Recommends integer minor units (cents) or a decimal type for money, not floats
Assigns HIGH or BLOCKER for the money-correctness risk
